newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Berlian says will revise up 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Berlian says will revise up 1996 profit.

text.p: Indonesia shipping firm PT Berlian Laju Tanker said on Monday the company will soon revise up its 1996 net profit forecast of 12.5 billion rupiah following government tax breaks to bolster the domestic shipping industry.

"Our net target for 1996 is 12.5 billion and EPS (earnings per share) of 213 rupiah, but soon we will revise those figures significantly up," Kevin Wong, corporate secretary of Berlian Laju Tanker, told Reuters.
Wong declined to give details, saying the company will announce its nine-month result later in November.
"From the nine-month result, investors can figure out the number for 1996. It's not appropriate to give the figures now," he said.

Wong said the tax breaks announced in May, and effective from last January 25, provided the main impetus for the profit growth. There was also the possibility of receiving some contracts from state-owned oil company Pertamina.
"Previously we were not really competitive compared to foreign shipping companies, but now we are benefiting," he said.
Wong also said the company sees a 35 percent profit growth in 1997 and expects to maintain average growth of 38 percent a year for the next three years.-- Jakarta newsroom +6221-384-6364
